issue.title: cross_val_score and GridSearchCV should allow for missing values encoded as NaNs

labels.name: Easy
labels.description: Well-defined and straightforward way to resolve

issue.body:
Assume you want to evaluate or grid search the parameters of the following pipeline

``` python
from sklearn.preprocessing import Imputer
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline

p = Pipeline([
    ('imputer', Imputer(strategy='media', missing_values='NaN')),
    ('classifier', LogisticRegression(C=1)),
])
```

At the moment it is not possible as the `cross_val_score` and `GridSearchCV` tools call `check_arrays` internally which raises an exception if there are `NaN` values in the data.

I think we should add `allow_nans=False` parameter to `check_arrays`, `cross_val_score` and `GridSearchCV` to make it possible to the user to disable the check for nans and hence allow our imputing pipeline to work as expected.

body: @ogrisel pointed out in #3044 that `cross_val_score` suffers from the same problem.

I'm trying to fix this by following the suggestions from @ogrisel in #3044, i.e. adding an argument `allow_nans=False` to `check_arrays`, which disables the call to `_assert_all_finite` when set to `True`. `BaseSearchCV` will then call `check_arrays` with `allow_nans=True`.

Several functions responsible for cross validation also suffers from the same problem, namely `cross_val_score`, `permutation_test_score`, and `train_test_split` as they all call `check_arrays` internally before the fitting of estimator happens. To fix the problem, I think they should all call `check_arrays` with `allow_nans=True`. The purpose of calling `check_arrays` in these places is to make sure that the input arrays have consistent dimensions and correct sparse format if applicable. It is the responsibility of the estimator to check the whether the fitting data contains NaNs, and then only panic if it cannot handle it.

Does this approach make sense? Let me know if I missed anything.

It makes sense, but it does add a lot of complexity in various places to support one particular use case. We could alternatively not add these parameters and just allows NaNs through; the estimators will catch them.

Ping @GaelVaroquaux and @jnothman who may be interested in this API issue.

@larsmans, I think you are suggesting roughly the same thing as @YS-L, as long as you believe that  the cross-validation functions should still be calling `check_arrays` (and I think they must, before selecting folds), and as long as you believe that in most cases `check_arrays` should require finite data (I don't see much reason to change this behaviour).

I think the default behavior of `check_arrays` should remain the same, as this function is called in quite a number of places, including those "real" estimators which indeed require finite data.

A quick check by changing the behavior of `check_arrays` to allow NaNs by default shows that 44 tests failed, all complaining that "Estimator doesn't check for NaN and inf in fit".
@YS-L @jnothman I'm sorry, I think I misread the suggestion. Yes, this seems like the right thing to do. I thought you wanted that parameter on public APIs.

issue.title: [MRG+2] FIX: Add allow_nans option to check_arrays
issue.body:
In some cases (in particular during grid search and cross validation)
check_arrays should not panic when seeing NaNs in the input arrays.
Fixes #2774 and #3044.
